baseline.policy: The original app calls the original E.extend exactly eight times with one continuous seeded RNG. It chooses the greatest linear roundProfile favorable count, treating a null profile as -1, retaining the first candidate on ties.

method.exactFinalScoring: X.coverageExact on saved rows plus final new batch, including nonlinear totals and all 25 tickets.
method.storageAndBatchChecks: Both paths must leave saved rows unchanged, return no saved duplicates, and produce a linear new batch accepted by P.analyze.
method.timing: One old run then one current run per seed; generation time excludes the separate final validation. These local single-run timings include uneven JIT warmup and do not predict browser device latency.

limitations: Both generators receive the same frozen baseline-templates.json. This isolates the additional-generation engine change; it does not measure later production template improvements.
Twenty deterministic cases are a small regression benchmark, not proof of an average or universal gain.

Matching seeds only matches the initial RNG state. Refinement and early returns consume different random sequences, so candidate sets can differ and an individual current result can be worse than the old app result.
The extension search accepts strict improvements over its own retained baseline. This does not by itself guarantee dominance over all eight candidates selected by the previous app.
This compares overlap coverage for the same number of purchased games; it makes no claim of predicting drawn numbers or increasing one ticket's jackpot probability.
